\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{طوفان} (tufân)}{طوفان (tufân)}]{\fa{طوفان} (tufân) — a storm}

\label{lesson:FA-C330-tufan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to leak, then the Persian for ash.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{طوفان}}
\textbf{\fa{طوفان}} (\emph{tufân}) — \textquotedblleft{}a storm\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{طوفان} \fa{درخت} \fa{های} \fa{زیادی} \fa{را} \fa{انداخت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tufân derakht-hâ-ye ziyâdi râ andâkht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The storm brought down a lot of trees.
\end{quote}

Also \emph{tufân-e shen} \textquotedblleft{}a sandstorm\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tufân} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṭūfān}, \textquotedblleft{}storm, typhoon\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tufân}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tufân}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tufân}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to leak, then the Persian for ash, then say \emph{tufân} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{غرق} \fa{شدن} (gharq shodan)}{غرق شدن (gharq shodan)}]{\fa{غرق} \fa{شدن} (gharq shodan) — to drown; to sink}

\label{lesson:FA-C330-gharq-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for ash, then the Persian for a storm.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{غرق} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{غرق} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{gharq shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to drown; to sink\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قایق} \fa{در} \fa{دریا} \fa{غرق} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Qâyeq dar daryâ gharq shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boat sank in the sea.
\end{quote}

Of people \textquotedblleft{}to drown\textquotedblright{}, of boats \textquotedblleft{}to sink\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{gharq mishavad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gharq} \textquotedblleft{}drowning, sinking\textquotedblright{} is borrowed from Arabic, of the root of \emph{gharaqa} \textquotedblleft{}to drown\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists the Arabic verb). \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gharq shodan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gharq shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{gharq shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for ash, then the Persian for a storm, then say \emph{gharq shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{غرق} \fa{شدن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To drown; to sink\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سقوط} \fa{کردن} (soqut kardan)}{سقوط کردن (soqut kardan)}]{\fa{سقوط} \fa{کردن} (soqut kardan) — to crash down, to fall (from a height)}

\label{lesson:FA-C330-soqut-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a storm, then the Persian for to drown.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سقوط} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{سقوط} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{soqut kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to crash down, to fall (from a height)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هواپیما} \fa{در} \fa{کوه} \fa{سقوط} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Havâpeymâ dar kuh soqut kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The plane crashed in the mountains.
\end{quote}

For planes, buildings and governments. Present \emph{soqut mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{soqut} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{suqūṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}a fall\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{soqut kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{soqut kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{soqut kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a storm, then the Persian for to drown, then say \emph{soqut kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{سقوط} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To crash down, to fall (from a height)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{هشدار} (hoshdâr)}{هشدار (hoshdâr)}]{\fa{هشدار} (hoshdâr) — a warning, an alert}

\label{lesson:FA-C330-hoshdar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to drown, then the Persian for to crash down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{هشدار}}
\textbf{\fa{هشدار}} (\emph{hoshdâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a warning, an alert\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{رادیو} \fa{هشدار} \fa{طوفان} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Râdiyo hoshdâr-e tufân dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The radio gave a storm warning.
\end{quote}

\emph{hosh} \textquotedblleft{}mind, attention\textquotedblright{} + \emph{dâr} \textquotedblleft{}holding\textquotedblright{}: keep your mind on it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hoshdâr} joins \emph{hosh} \textquotedblleft{}mind, attention\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Middle Persian (EtymDB), and \emph{dâr-}, the present stem of \emph{dâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to hold\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hoshdâr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hoshdâr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{hoshdâr}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to drown, then the Persian for to crash down, then say \emph{hoshdâr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{هشدار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A warning, an alert\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{هشدار} \fa{دادن} (hoshdâr dâdan)}{هشدار دادن (hoshdâr dâdan)}]{\fa{هشدار} \fa{دادن} (hoshdâr dâdan) — to warn}

\label{lesson:FA-C330-hoshdar-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to crash down, then the Persian for a warning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{هشدار} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{هشدار} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{hoshdâr dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to warn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پلیس} \fa{به} \fa{مردم} \fa{هشدار} \fa{داد} \fa{که} \fa{از} \fa{خانه} \fa{بیرون} \fa{نروند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Polis be mardom hoshdâr dâd ke az khâne birun naravand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police warned people not to go out of their homes.
\end{quote}

The person warned takes \emph{be}; the warning follows in a \emph{ke} clause with the subjunctive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hoshdâr dâdan} joins the native noun \emph{hoshdâr} \textquotedblleft{}a warning\textquotedblright{} with \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to crash down, then the Persian for a warning, then say \emph{hoshdâr dâdan} again
